key_insight: Near-equilibrium accuracy did not guarantee reliable fatigue behavior: NequIP predicted an intrinsic stacking fault energy about seven times lower than EAM and substantially more plastic deformation.
engineering_relevance: Interatomic potentials used for fatigue simulations need validation under driven, nonequilibrium conditions, not just near-equilibrium benchmarks.
method: Compare EAM and the NequIP foundational potential on near-equilibrium properties.
Apply fatigue cycling to a nanoscale flaw modeled after the classical Griffith crack problem.
Analyze per-atom energy distributions after loading.
evidence_signal: Both potentials closely matched reference data for many near-equilibrium properties, but their post-loading energy distributions differed most far above thermally accessible energies.
watch_item: Memory-related crashes and silent extrapolation are practical risks when deploying foundational interatomic potentials.
paper_title: Emergent Fatigue Dynamics from Foundational Interatomic Potentials
